quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Research shows that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When another motorcycle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left side of the lane.
Ride in the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other rider from returning to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks up, how do you regain control?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Speed up while keeping the brake on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. On a good road surface with the rear brake locked, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops completely.

questions.question: A motorcycle windshield:

options.text: Is a good replacement for a face shield.
Is a good replacement for goggles.
Does not protect your eyes from wind.
Does not protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not enough instead of a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: When your weight moves forward during braking, you:

options.text: Can press the front brake harder.
Should press the front brake less hard.
Can press the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can press the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It uses less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
A close group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: A close group reaches the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group uses less road space, is easier to see, and stays together better at traffic lights and when passing other vehicles.

questions.question: What formation should a group use when exiting a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is best for normal group riding, switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, what part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left side
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of the lane when passing on the left. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Follow closer to the car ahead.
Use the headlights of the car ahead to see the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the car ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and stay far behind other vehicles. Use their headlights to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed, especially when riding at night.

questions.question: When might you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. You need more distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or in heavy traffic when another car might cut in front of you.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcycles at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcycles, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane are better.
Improves grip for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcycles, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area is usually safe to ride on. The strip is normally only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When you speed up, a motorcycle with a sidecar will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is speeding up faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is a non-powered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you away from other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, and avoid road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a safe escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is used for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limits
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show rules like speed limits are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. Riders must follow these signs.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they appear to be:

options.text: Going faster than they actually are.
Going slower than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles look like they are going faster than they really are because of their small size.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes a lot of grip.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that takes a lot of grip to do safely. Do not swerve suddenly on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
Someone is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing someone on the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn a driver or pedestrian who might move into your path. If a nearby driver is following too closely, they might cut in front of you. Use your horn when passing a parked car with a driver inside, or when passing a pedestrian or cyclist. Do not use your horn just to draw attention to yourself.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of these except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently when carrying a passenger due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors.

questions.question: If road conditions require longer stopping distance, what should you do?

options.text: Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs longer to stop. Use at least a three-second following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does the lead rider mean by raising their left arm and pointing one finger?

options.text: The group will exit at the next turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger, it means the group should form a single-file line.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratches and become weak, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made to break easily during a crash.
They should not let any air pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratches and become weak, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic and will develop scratches and become weak over time. Replace them regularly for the best protection and comfort.
